questions.title: Can the frontier keep building larger AI systems?
questions.summary: Tracks the compute, capital, and physical capacity that makes future training and inference possible.
questions.what_would_change: A sustained break in frontier-compute growth, or verified energized power and chip capacity that contradicts announced build plans.

questions.title: Are systems becoming more capable on real, long-horizon tasks?
questions.summary: Favors task completion and independently evaluated autonomy over broad capability labels.
questions.what_would_change: Replicated, methodology-stable evaluations showing either durable long-horizon gains or a flattening after controls for evaluation gaming.

questions.title: Is AI accelerating the creation of better AI?
questions.summary: Direct public evidence is limited: company reports show task-specific contributions, while independent causal evidence remains adjacent to frontier AI R&D.
questions.what_would_change: A repeated, independently audited measure of AI contribution to frontier research, plus verified successor-system work with limited human direction.

questions.title: Are algorithms improving capability faster than hardware scales?
questions.summary: Separates capability gains from additional hardware and records the vintage of the underlying methodology.
questions.what_would_change: A current, transparent fixed-capability efficiency series or evidence that observed improvements no longer transfer across tasks.

questions.title: How much capable AI is actually being deployed and used?
questions.summary: Distinguishes spending and revenue signals from verified autonomous deployment and economic use.
questions.what_would_change: Audited adoption, utilization, and productivity series that can be separated from vendor revenue and announced investment.

questions.title: Does greater capability translate into harmful real-world power?
questions.summary: Tests whether cognitive performance converts into practical cyber, bio, persuasion, or resource-acquisition advantage.
questions.what_would_change: Independently documented incidents or controlled evaluations that establish a reliable capability-to-impact link, including effective defenses.

questions.title: Can powerful systems be controlled, monitored, and reliably evaluated?
questions.summary: Tracks the hard-to-measure gap between a model appearing safe in evaluation and remaining controllable in deployment.
questions.what_would_change: Independent safety evaluations, robust behavioral monitoring, and evidence that mitigations hold under realistic deployment pressure.

questions.title: Can institutions impose and enforce meaningful constraints?
questions.summary: Measures enforceable action rather than policy announcements, and keeps coordination as an open question.
questions.what_would_change: Verified implementation and enforcement evidence across relevant jurisdictions, especially where commercial incentives conflict with restraint.

questions.title: Are influential trajectory forecasts surviving contact with reality?
questions.summary: Compares dated, attributed claims with their intended measurements while preserving scenarios, conditions, and revisions.
questions.what_would_change: More comparable resolved probabilistic forecasts, pre-registered scoring rules, and direct measures for currently proxy-scored claims.

questions.title: Are real-world harms and near misses increasing?
questions.summary: A deliberately visible coverage gap: incidents and near misses need a curated, independently verifiable series before they can be trended.
questions.what_would_change: A transparent incident taxonomy with primary documentation, severity criteria, and explicit coverage limits.
